result.killer: No product found that does the whole job. The closest are partial: (1) gastouderbureau admin suites Tamina, Opvangapp (De Gastoudercentrale), Portabase, Konnect and Bitcare. The Tamina and Opvangapp pages list hours, invoicing, contracts and documents, but nothing on PE, coaching or the work plan, and either vendor could add it easily. (2) PE course platforms that already give certificates and a bureau view: Leerlijn Gastouderopvang (bureaus can enrol their gastouders, certificates for the GGD) and Gastouderland's Kinderwijs TV (EUR 99.95, the bureau sees progress and certificates). Enforcement is also deferred: the GGD does not check hours in 2026, and the first assessed year is 2027.
result.reason: Nothing I found kills it. The bureau admin suites (Tamina, Opvangapp) don't mention tracking PE or coaching, and there is no free state tool. But the market is small and shrinking: about 16,600 gastouders in 2024, down from 33,585 in 2016. An older Kamerbrief says the 10 largest bureaus hold about 50% of gastouders. I couldn't find how many bureaus there are. The feature is thin and the current billing suites, or PE course providers like Leerlijn and Gastouderland that already issue certificates, could easily add it. Hours enforcement starts with calendar year 2027, so there's little urgency now. As a stand-alone product for a solo founder it is weak. It works better as an add-on or a way into general bureau software, where the competition is real.

result.killer: MijnEML is a dedicated, packaged informatieplicht reporting service and a Rabobank partner; Rabobank clients get EUR 100 off its packages. Rabobank's energiebesparingsplicht page says this, as reported by search snippets; the page itself returned 403, and I did not reach MijnEML's own site or prices. Greenchoice's Energiebespaarregelaar is a paid licence for an online saving tool plus energy-saving advice per location, offered to "facilitate" the informatieplicht. The KHN DEB tool and its energy partner COMCAM cover hospitality firms. RVO's free XML upload and intermediary authorisation already let advisers file for several clients.
result.reason: The claim that no dedicated product exists is wrong. MijnEML (via Rabobank) and Greenchoice's Energiebespaarregelaar both sell productised EML/informatieplicht help. Sector bodies (KHN DEB/COMCAM, MKB DEB) and RVO's free XML hulpbestand cover much of the rest. The deadline is also uncertain. The 2027 revision is still a draft, laid before the Eerste Kamer on 1 Sep 2026 and due in force 1 Jul 2027. The old duty for those who reported in 2023 lapses from 1 Dec 2027, and responsibility splits between building owners and operators. No first reporting date under the new rules was found, so the one-off spike may move. The duty is real and enforced with penalty payments (dwangsom), and earlier rounds had low compliance, so a niche remains for a sector-specific helper. But the market is contested, and it peaks only once every 4 years.

result.competitor: Not established. Searches in Dutch ('gastouderbureau software', 'software voor gastouderbureaus', administration and portal queries) returned only government pages and generic training software such as Coachview. Childcare suites that came up (KidsKonnect/Flexkids, KindPlanner, KOVnet) target kindercentra and BSO. The KOVnet site does not mention gastouderbureaus, permanente educatie, coaching or the work plan. No free state tool for logging the hours was found. Niche gastouderbureau administration and billing software almost certainly exists but was not reached, so whether it already logs training and coaching hours is unverified.
result.duty: Confirmed and in force since 1 Jul 2026. The Besluit kwaliteit gastouderbureaus was folded into the Besluit kwaliteit kinderopvang (Wet kinderopvang). The rules: 7 h of permanente educatie per gastouder per year (Regeling art. 25(1)(b)); at least 3 h of coaching per gastouder per year from each bureau, given by the bureau's pedagogisch beleidsmedewerker, with the coaching agreement in writing and signed; a pedagogical work plan per voorziening; a pedagogical module for gastouders who start after 1 Jul 2026 (current LRK-registered gastouders are exempt); at most 2 bureaus per gastouder; own children up to age 8 count toward the cap. The GGD inspects and the municipality enforces under the Wet kinderopvang. Ondernemersplein names no specific fine amounts.
result.market: No current LRK count found. A parliamentary document from 2008-09 counted about 700 gastouderbureaus. A consultation response citing LRK data says 12,582 gastouders stopped between Mar 2018 and Mar 2023 (-41%). A Nieuwegein council motion says active gastouders fell more than 40% between Jan 2020 and Jan 2025. About 80,000 children were in gastouderopvang in mid-2024, and about 23% of gastouders are over 60. That suggests a few hundred bureaus as paying buyers and roughly 15-25k gastouders (estimate, unverified).
result.reason: The duty is real. Under Dutch law in force since 1 Jul 2026, every gastouder needs 7 h of permanente educatie a year, at least 3 h of signed coaching a year from each bureau, and a pedagogical work plan per voorziening. A gastouder may join at most 2 bureaus. The GGD checks compliance. In six searches and one vendor check (KOVnet, which covers daycare and BSO only) I found no product that tracks these hours. Search coverage of niche gastouderbureau admin vendors was poor, so competition is not ruled out. The market is small and shrinking: there are probably a few hundred bureaus (a parliamentary paper counted 700 in 2008-09), and gastouders fell about 41% over five years. Willingness to pay is likely low. An admin vendor could add this as a feature.

result.competitor: LegionellaDossier (Dutch): app, Bluetooth temperature sensor, online environment with all control measures, digital logbooks, flushing schedules, QR asset tagging and dashboards. It claims that 75% of Dutch legionella consultancies are partners (vendor claim). BRL 6010 consultancies (Kiwa and others) deliver the plan and logbook as a service. UK tools (TEAMS online logbook, Legionella GO, Howlett app) and generic form apps (GoCanvas, Lumiform templates) exist but matter less here. A paper or Excel logbook following the plan also meets the rule.
result.duty: Confirmed in the Drinkwaterbesluit (BWBR0030111), version in force from 15-08-2026. Art. 35(1) lists the priority premises: care institutions, lodging (c1/c2), asylum centres, cells, pools of at least 2 m2 and deeper than 0.5 m, campsites (g), marinas (h), truckstops, petrol stations and roadside restaurants with public showers (i), and saunas. Art. 37: the risk analysis must be done by a BRL 6010-certified firm and redone within 3 months of relevant changes. Art. 38: a management plan, also by a certified firm. Art. 40: the owner carries out the measures and keeps a logbook for 3 years, available to the inspector. Art. 41(3): notify the inspector (ILT) immediately above 1,000 cfu/l. Art. 43: sample every 6 months, or once a year if the system is in use 7 months a year or less. Sports clubs are not priority premises; only the general zorgplicht applies. Penalty provisions were not read on the page. I found no 2026 change to the legionella chapter; the new standard based on Legionella pneumophila and the EU Drinking Water Directive changes were not verified as in force.
result.market: Not verified. CBS reports 52.2M guests at hotels, campsites and holiday parks in 2025, but the search did not give counts of premises. The number of campsites, marinas and truckstops would come from CBS StatLine table 82062, which I did not reach. No national count of priority premises was found; the only figure is an old 2009 count of 480 hospital-type institutions.
result.reason: The duty is real and in force. Drinkwaterbesluit (version in force from 15-08-2026) art. 35 covers campsites (g), marinas (h), truckstops, petrol stations and roadside restaurants with public showers (i), lodging (c), saunas and pools. Sports clubs are not covered and have only the general zorgplicht. The core software job, a digital logbook with planning, reminders and sampling records, is already done in Dutch by LegionellaDossier. It sells an app, a Bluetooth thermometer and a subscription, and claims that 75% of Dutch legionella consultancies are partners. That is a vendor claim. The risk analysis and management plan must come from BRL 6010-certified firms, which also own the client relationship. Seasonal campsites only need to sample once a year. What's left for a newcomer is a thin logbook layer that competes with the consultancies' own tools.

result.competitor: Free state tools: RVO eLoket/Mijn RVO filing form, the RVO Wetchecker energiebesparing, the RVO Hulpbestand XML-upload IPEB (v1.4.0, recommended for more than 5 locations, with an XSD schema), and the intermediary authorisation form, so advisers can already file for clients. Also MKB-Nederland's Platform DEB and wattjemoetweten.nl with EML guidance, and SRA advieswijzers for accountants. Consultants and installers offer the filing as a service. In 5 searches I found no dedicated SaaS or fixed-price productised filing service for SMEs. That search was not exhaustive, and I did not look for sector-specific EML vendors in depth.
result.duty: Energy-saving duty and information duty (informatieplicht energiebesparing) under the Activiteitenbesluit transitional law and the Bal/Bbl. Locations using at least 50,000 kWh electricity or 25,000 m3 natural gas equivalent per year report once every 4 years to RVO which EML measures they have taken. Next final deadline is 1 Dec 2027 for locations that had the duty on 1 Dec 2023. The drijver van de inrichting stays responsible until then. Enforcement is by the omgevingsdienst on behalf of the competent authority, which can demand improvements and enforce. RVO's page gives no fine amounts; I did not confirm the dwangsom (penalty payment) mentioned in the claim. IPLO says the updated duty takes effect 1 Jul 2027, but the Bal/Bbl and Omgevingsregeling amendments were still in consultation (the latter until 19 Aug 2026), with publication planned for early 2027. The payback period goes from 5 to 7 years and the thresholds stay at 50,000 kWh. The 100,000 kWh threshold raise is not part of the proposal.
result.market: The government estimated about 50,000-60,000 obligated firms for the first round (2019), of which about 22,000 filed by the deadline (accountant.nl). An Activiteitenbesluit amendment's explanatory note cites about 100,000 firms and institutions. Provincie Utrecht alone estimates about 5,800. The exact number is unknown because energy suppliers do not share consumption data, and many obligated firms are not on the authorities' radar.
result.reason: The duty is real and in force. RVO confirms that locations using at least 50,000 kWh or 25,000 m3 gas must report every 4 years, with the next deadline on 1 Dec 2027. The omgevingsdienst enforces it. The rule changes (payback period 7 years, new EML, in force 1 Jul 2027) are still consultation drafts, so whatever is built has to follow a moving target. The core filing job is a free RVO eLoket form, and RVO also gives away an XML bulk-upload helper and lets intermediaries file. Accountants, installers and consultants already offer the service. I found no dedicated SME SaaS. Pain comes once every 4 years and the form is short, so willingness to pay is low. Reaching buyers through installers or accountants is the plausible channel.

result.competitor: ComplianceWise Grub: endorsed by SRA, Novak and Auxilium, claims 500+ firms, starts from a KvK number; prices are not public (its terms have a 'Tarieven Diensten' section, figures not seen). SRA Zkr: the full Wwft process, including periodic re-review, PEP/sanctions checks and CRM/DMS links. In 2019 the older SRA/Dapas tool cost EUR 20-35 per user per month (a stale figure). Also: CaseWare WWFT+ (Wwft app launched 2019, current status not checked), Blinqx, AdminPulse (practice-management tool with Wwft client-data tracking), PKIsigning (ID verification), and Fiscount/NOAB e-learnings. Not verified: any vendor's AMLR-ready release, and any published price for a one-person office.
result.duty: Confirmed. The Wwft is in force now and covers administratie- and belastingadvieskantoren, including one-person firms. Duties: client due diligence including UBO identification, a firm-level risk policy, unusual-transaction reporting to the FIU, training and record retention. The BFT supervises and can fine; the claim's EUR 10,000 fine example was not re-checked. AMLR (Reg. 2024/1624) applies directly from 10 Jul 2027 (SRA). It adds file refresh within 1 year for high-risk clients and 5 years for others, a UBO test at 25% or more, sanctions screening, named compliance roles and new periodic data-point reporting to the supervisor. AMLD6 will be transposed through the Iwt; the SRA article gives no status or timing for it. In January 2026 NOAB and the BFT agreed that Wwft supervision becomes part of the NOAB quality mark.
result.market: A BFT position paper (March 2026) says the BFT supervises about 50,000 Wwft institutions with about 50 FTE. That figure covers notaries, accountants, tax advisers and administratiekantoren together. Sources say there are 'tienduizenden' (tens of thousands) of administratie- and belastingadvieskantoren. No exact count for small administratiekantoren was found.
result.reason: The duty is real. The Wwft applies to administratiekantoren and bookkeepers, including one-person firms, which cannot use the process exemption. The AMLR applies from 10 Jul 2027 and adds file refresh cycles (1 year for high-risk clients, 5 years for others), a UBO test at 25% or more, sanctions screening and periodic data reporting to the supervisor. Several mature tools already do the core job. ComplianceWise Grub is endorsed by SRA, Novak and Auxilium, claims 500+ firms, and says a firm needs only a KvK number to start. SRA's Zkr covers acceptance, risk analysis, periodic re-review (hertoetsing) and PEP/sanctions checks. CaseWare WWFT+, Blinqx and AdminPulse are also on the market. Since Jan 2026, NOAB's quality mark covers Wwft supervision through an arrangement with the BFT, which channels members to established tooling. The only possible gap is an AMLR-ready product with low published pricing. I couldn't verify that gap: no vendor publishes prices, and I didn't check AMLR readiness.

result.competitor: Free tools: the SZW webmodule Beoordeling arbeidsrelatie, hetjuistecontract.nl (10 questions) and the TeamZlab ZZP check, which uses an outdated EUR 33 threshold. Checklists: Declercq (recommends keeping KvK, VAT and insurance records per zzp'er and repeating the check every six months), Techniek Nederland, KHN and Rendement. Consultancy: the BDO 'Blik op de Arbeidsrelatie' risk dashboard. Other alternatives: Deel (misclassification audit, employer of record), Loyal and Nedflex staffing alternatives, and payroll providers. Stichting ZZP-erkend: the only sources found date from about 2012 and describe a free, Rabobank-funded VAR/KvK/VAT dossier. VAR was abolished, so the scheme is probably defunct, but this is unconfirmed. No dedicated SME SaaS was found for keeping per-zzp'er evidence for the presumption. Not checked: whether booking platforms in the low-rate sectors (horeca, care) already bundle these checks.
result.duty: Art. 7:610aa BW (Stb. 2026, 158; commencement Stb. 2026, 207) creates a rebuttable presumption that work paid at most EUR 36 per hour is done under an employment contract. The minister can index the amount. It is in force from 31 Dec 2026 and does not apply when the client is a private person not acting for a business. It does not create an explicit record-keeping or filing duty: the hirer bears the burden of proof in civil disputes. Tax side: the Belastingdienst has enforced against false self-employment since 2025. It gives no verzuimboetes in 2026 but can claim back payroll taxes (naheffingen) and impose vergrijpboetes for intent or gross negligence, with full fines expected from 2027 (KNAB, Accountancy van Morgen). The Zelfstandigenwet has been in internetconsultatie from 1 to 29 Oct 2026 with a 1 Jan 2028 target. It is not law, and its safe-harbour proof rules (third-party statement, AOV or pension provision) are not final. Claims of EUR 38 come from SRA reports of the parliamentary stage; the published law text says EUR 36.
result.market: No register-based count of hirers was found. A 2025 CBS business survey (with KvK, EIB, MKB-Nederland and VNO-NCW) found that about a third of firms do not hire zzp'ers, so roughly two-thirds do. Over 42% of 2024 hirers expected to hire fewer in 2025 because of enforcement (Taxlive). The share hiring at or below EUR 36/h is not quantified, but it is concentrated in care, childcare, horeca, cleaning, transport and construction trades. That probably means tens of thousands of firms, but this is an unverified estimate.
result.reason: The trigger is real. Art. 7:610aa BW (Stb. 2026, 158) starts on 31 Dec 2026 (Stb. 2026, 207), and the threshold in the law text is EUR 36/h, not 38. Belastingdienst enforcement continues. No verzuimboetes in 2026, but vergrijpboetes are possible, with full fines expected from 2027. It is a civil burden-of-proof shift rather than a filing duty, so the pain is driven by risk and is not strictly mandatory. The Zelfstandigenwet is still a draft. ZZP-erkend looks like a 2012-era VAR scheme. No dedicated SME dossier SaaS was found; the alternatives are free tools (SZW module, hetjuistecontract), checklists, BDO/Deel and platforms. Low-rate hirers are price-sensitive, and a vendor faces liability risk if it declares a hire 'safe'. The revive of K21 is justified.

The duty is real: the CDT has applied since 1 Jul 2025, with a transition to 1 Jan 2028. But the CDT is itself the state system, and the operator chooses an ILT-connected ICT supplier's device or app. The existing BCT vendors (Euphoria/Cabman, Neone, Quipment, per Computable) are the natural CDT sellers, and ILT keeps a list of connected ICT providers. A new product would need ILT certification and would compete with them. The change also removes the card-swap costs. I found no penalty figures, no named CDT vendor list and no count of taxi firms (searches returned none), so those stay unverified. Buyer is small taxi firms; the product is a one-off migration, not a recurring workflow.

Duty is real but only partly mandatory. The art. 437 Sr purchase register applies in all municipalities. Copper cash purchases need the seller's ID document recorded (Stb 2012-480). DOR is mandatory only where a municipality designates it. The national DOR bill 36 036 passed the Tweede Kamer on 2 June 2026, but the Eerste Kamer has not voted and the start date is set by royal decree (secondary summary, not opened). I found no scrap-specific software. The free police DOR and municipal Opkopersloket probably cover the core job. Market size not found (no register count; KvK SBI or MRF would be needed). Scrap firms likely run ERP/weighbridge systems, so the opportunity is a niche DOR integration. Weak, small market.

Duty is real: Reg. (EG) 852/2004 registration per location. Per Ondernemersplein, businesses registered before 10 March 2026 must re-register in MijnNVWA, then confirm yearly; NVWA checks this at inspection. Free state portal (eHerkenning/DigiD) with reminder email does the whole job. No fee, penalty or end date found, and no volume figure. The task is a one-form login per location, so there is little recurring pain and little reason to pay. Wide buyer base, but a weak product. No commercial helper was found in one search. Not checked: KHN or KNS hand-holding, and the KvK or NVWA count of registered food businesses.

result.competitor: Smoobu and other channel managers; Airbnb and Booking.com number checks; free municipal registration portals
result.duty: Register with the municipality where it opts in, and show the registration number in every listing. Platforms must refuse listings without a number and share data with authorities under EU 2024/1028.
result.market: Not found. No host count from a register or statistic; the Netherlands has roughly 1,000 STR hosts per large city but this is unverified.
result.reason: The duty is real but weak for a standalone product. Hosts must register where a municipality opts in (Wet toeristische verhuur, in force since 1 Jan 2021; Amsterdam and Utrecht do). Fines are up to about 8,700 EUR, and Amsterdam has used higher amounts. The Raad van State cut one Amsterdam fine to 2,900 EUR. The EU 2024/1028 data duties fall on platforms and authorities, not hosts. Dutch alignment (Stb. 2026, 266) is not yet in force, and no date was found. Hosts register once for free through a municipal portal, so the workflow is a one-off, not recurring. Airbnb and Booking verify numbers themselves, and channel managers such as Smoobu cover listings. No national host portal was confirmed. Market size was not found.

Duty is real: Tabaks- en rookwarenwet amendment in force 1 Jul 2026; owners of tobacco and vape outlets must register with the NVWA via a digital portal using eHerkenning; an administrative fine applies. Annual renewal comes only from a 2025 Kamer debate and is unconfirmed in the final rule. The fine amount and the deadline for existing sellers were not found. Competition: the free state NVWA portal does the core job, and I found no vendor. The product would only wrap a one-off form, and the market is shrinking (about 10,000 outlets in 2024, about 1,500 specialist shops by 2032). Willingness to pay is low and the pain is small. Score stays low.

The SCE exists and had a 2026 window (2 Mar to 1 Oct 2026, now closed; 15-year subsidy, solar and wind only). But it is voluntary: it is a subsidy application, not a mandatory recurring duty with a penalty. It is also a one-off application per project, not a yearly workflow. Only about 696 co-ops exist (Lokale Energie Monitor 2025), with 66 new projects in 2025 and 137 SCE grants awarded, so the buyer pool is small, volunteer-run and unlikely to pay. No dedicated software turned up, but HIER and Energie Samen offer free guidance. I did not verify penalties or the controller-report duties, so the verdict is unverifiable. Weak fit.

The duty is real. Besluit UPV textiel has applied since 1 Jul 2023, with 2025 targets. Producers must register with Rijkswaterstaat within 6 weeks and report yearly before 1 Aug. From 2026 the report must also say whether targets were met. Foreign sellers need a Dutch authorised representative. ILT enforces, and the Wet Economische Delicten applies. I found no small-firm threshold. Competition is heavy: producer organisations (Stichting UPV Textiel, ERP Netherlands with a 2026 fee of EUR 0.24/kg, EY support) already do registration, reporting and collection as a bundled service, so there is little software gap. Market size is not found in a register. Pain is low for members, and a solo vendor would only be a reseller or wrapper. Not checked: the detailed Click & Comply scope.

The duty is real. Bal paragraph 4.94 (IPLO) requires BRL SIKB 7800-certified installation and maintenance, a yearly check of electronic leak detection, monthly pot checks with at least a yearly logbook entry, and periodic inspection by accredited bodies under AS SIKB 6800/6700. The claim's "BIC" and the penalty were not found (the IPLO page does not cover them). Inspection bodies must register results in a central SIKB system, so the compliance record already sits with certified parties. Installers and inspectors hold the certificates and the schedule, which leaves little for a third-party tool. No Dutch software for this was found. Market data is weak: about 4,100 fuel stations (Bovag, shrinking), and no count of farm or contractor tanks. Buyers are fragmented, with low willingness to pay. Several steps are done by certified firms, not the owner.

The duty is real. Stb 2024-46 makes it mandatory from 1 Apr 2024 to list on-site leidinggevenden (horeca only) on the licence aanhangsel. Changes are notified to the municipality under art. 30a Alcoholwet, using paper or PDF forms with a fee. Paracommercial clubs must keep a register of IVA-trained volunteers. I found no dedicated software, only free model reglementen, municipal forms and KHN or NOC*NSF e-learning. Weak points: events are irregular and low frequency (staff changes, not an annual filing). The filing goes to about 340 different municipalities with different forms, and there is little to automate beyond a form. Clubs pay little. Market size was not found (no national count). Competition from roster tools was only lightly checked. Score 3.
